(1) MRA has sample complexity $O(1/\mathrm{snr}^3)$ in the low SNRs regime; (2) the heterogeneous version has a similar sample complexity, which is the first theoretical result for this model; (3) the proofs rely on a novel technique that we call "spectral alignment," which may have applications beyond MRA.

we provide a first step towards developing statistical theory for heterogeneous Cryo-EM.

we prove that, in MRA, a single sample can already provide a good estimate of the unknown signal, and that a large number of samples is required to recover a generic unknown signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the low SNRs that are common in practice, the statistical complexity of MRA and other related models is significantly higher than that of the standard additive Gaussian noise model.
